headline: Agreed to form a stakeholder group on the commercial hot water heating exemption expiring June 2027; approved June and amended July minutes.
summary: The committee discussed battery storage, EV charging, renewable diesel, and its FY 27 workplan. It agreed to form a stakeholder group to evaluate the commercial hot water exemption, which expires in June 2027. It approved the June minutes and the amended July minutes, both unanimously.
decisions: Approved the June meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved the amended July meeting minutes unanimously.
Agreed to form a stakeholder group to evaluate whether the commercial hot water exemption should be extended.
Decided to focus the festival booth on balcony solar and resilient adaptation content instead of window heat pumps.

plain_text:
South Burlington Energy Committee
August 25, 2026
The South Burlington Energy Committee held a regular meeting on Tuesday, August 25th in
Room 301, 180 Market St. and by Zoom remote participation.
Members present: Jean Sebastien Chaulot, Steve Crowley (Chair), Ethan Goldman, Leendert
Huisman, Fred Kosnitsky, MJ Reale (Vice-Chair),
Also present: Bettina Miguez (Climate Action Manager), Lou Bresee (Energy Project Manager),
Member of the public: none
Welcome and Agenda review 
Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda: none
Updates From Committee Members/Events and conferences attended:
Leendert attended Net Zero Fest - VEEP program has valuable educational materials about
home insulation, but he is concerned about the continued promotion of wood burning as
climate-neutral. He registered for the EAN network summit and a presentation proposal.
The group discussed the conflict between reducing greenhouse gases and replacing fossil
fuels with renewables, with differing views about the pros and cons of transitioning from coal
and oil to wood heating, like enhanced boiler heating systems. 
Steve mentioned that there is an upcoming community leadership summit in Castleton on
October 6th and some of the content is on building local resilience in the face of climate
change.   https://www.vtrural.org/summit/
Fred and Leendert are involved with Third Act VT.
Ethan attended a summer conference with the American Council for Energy Efficient Economy
where they presented on a hybrid heat pump project with VGS and supported Chris Neme's
presentation on the impact of the renewable heating ordinance in South Burlington. He
explained that while there was interest in the ordinance, it may not effectively offset gas
consumption in homes with hybrid systems, potentially due to swap over temperature issues
with dual fuel systems. The team discussed next steps focusing on gathering information about
heat pump installations in new homes and researching potential changes to the ordinance or
code enforcement to improve effectiveness.
To do: Bettina asked Ethan to present more info on an upcoming SBEC meeting
The group also discussed battery technology and its potential applications, particularly in
managing grid imbalances caused by increased renewable energy and electric vehicle
adoption. They explored the challenges of battery implementation, including cost-effectiveness
and fire safety concerns, while noting that Green Mountain Power is already leading several
battery storage initiatives in Vermont. The discussion concluded with consideration of South
Burlington's potential role in battery pilot programs, focusing on identifying industrial accounts
that could benefit from battery storage solutions and exploring how the city could support
GMP's efforts through streamlined permitting and other measures.
Committee discussed the challenges of stabilizing new electric loads and mentioned that utility
companies handle most of this planning internally, with limited city involvement required. They
explored microgrids and emergency facility hardening as resilience measures, though noted
South Burlington's low outage frequency makes it less suitable for highlighting these efforts.
Staff Reports:  
Lou/Bettina provided updates on:
Advisory meeting that included Carrie, about EV charging in multi-unit buildings. GMP has a
pilot project with level 1.5 chargers, one of the HOAs is in South Burlington, to see if the slower
charging options may be sufficient for many users' needs. The consultant is currently working
on policy recommendations and guides based on property inventory and ordinances, with a
January deadline.
The building thermal implementation plan is being developed with community engagement
activities planned for October, including focus groups and advisory meetings to determine
priorities and draft edits. 
There are two UVM LIHI grant applications, one focusing on energy code enforcement and
another on a renewable diesel pilot program across the state.
Renewable diesel as a transition fuel - While it comes from biological materials like wood chips
and plants, it's processed differently than traditional biodiesel and produces cleaner fuel with
fewer CO2 emissions per kilogram. It was noted that South Burlington has not made any
commitments regarding this initiative yet, as they are waiting to see what happens with the
proposal. The discussion revealed that this would be a small pilot project using approximately
50,000 gallons annually, with a grant potentially covering the higher cost per gallon and student
analysis of economics and viability.
FY 27 Energy Committee Workplan
Here is the link:
https://www.southburlingtonvt.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/4807?fileID=6654
Committee discussed 4 work plan items:
Pilot outreach to landlords - this project is on hold because there is a new Assistant City
Manager who will be involved.
Renewable heating and hot water ordinance - Ordinance requires new construction to have
85% of human load served by renewable heat, with resistance electric heat being
unacceptable. The group discussed a current exemption for commercial hot water systems that
expires in June 2027, and they agreed to form a stakeholder group to evaluate whether the
exemption should be extended. The Energy Committee was tasked with identifying
stakeholders and conducting research to make a recommendation to council by April or May.
For the hot water issue, it was proposed convening a small group to work on recommendations
for the city council, potentially involving Efficiency Vermont for assistance. The discussion
included concerns about inspection processes and thermostat access, with suggestions that
they should first understand current inspection practices before proposing new requirements.
    To do: Start in October 2026 by forming a subcommittee and connect with Efficiency VT.
Link to ordinance:
https://library.municode.com/vt/south_burlington/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOO
R_CH38UT_ARTICLE._VIIHESEWAHESY
 CAP transportation implementation plan -  there are shared transportation options and noted
that the Energy Committee was more interested in tackling this topic than the Bike/Ped
committee. 
This can include the CATMA project.
The discussion included Local Motion regarding bike benefits for South Burlington, noting that
administration has shifted and there's potential for joint territory coverage. Bettina mentioned
that Ilona (Community Development Director) and Andy (Communications Director) are leading
a bus riding campaign; Keith was invited to learn about the initiative that will launch in
October/November and will need EC member outreach support.
Commercial energy audits??
Committee members decided to move on to next agenda items based on time.
Green Community Festival Update
Upcoming Green Community Festival, which will feature 35-40 exhibitors, 9-10 civic groups,
and four paid sponsors. The committee discussed volunteer needs for the festival, including
setup, staffing information tables, and traffic direction, with members committing to 4-hour shifts
during the event. They also reviewed materials for the festival booth, deciding to focus on
balcony solar and resilient adaptation content rather than window heat pumps due to market
availability concerns.
Approval of June Meeting Minutes - MJ moved to accept and Fred seconded.  Approved
unanimously by the group.
Approval of amended July Meeting Minutes - Fred moved to accept and Jean Sebastian
seconded.  Approved unanimously by the group.
The meeting was adjourned at 8:30 pm. Next meeting is September 23, 2026.
